# @ratmath/finance

> The mathematics of finance for RatMath: exact money, time value, loans, bonds, scenarios, uncertain inputs and repeated runs, portfolios, options and life contingencies. Part of the RatMath Shelf; numbers come from @ratmath/core (a peer dependency). ESM: `import * as finance from "@ratmath/finance"`.

Built from 0.2.0, commit a406eba plus uncommitted changes. `file:line` is relative to the package root (also node_modules/@ratmath/finance/); on GitHub: https://github.com/ratmath/finance/blob/a406eba/<file>#L<line>. Docs pages are under https://ratmath.com/finance/. Full types: index.d.ts.

Types: `type Amount = Rational | bigint | number | string`; `type Certified = Rational | RationalInterval`; `type Rounding = RoundingRule | number | RoundingMode | boolean | "none" | null`; `type DateLike = CalendarDate | string | [number, number, number]`; `type DayCount = "30/360" | "30E/360" | "actual/360" | "actual/365" | "actual/actual"`; `type Flows = Amount[] | { t?: Amount; amount: Amount }[]`; `type DatedFlows = { date: DateLike; amount: Amount }[]`; `type DepreciationMethod = "straight-line" | "declining-balance" | "sum-of-years-digits" | "units-of-production"`; `type When = number | string`

## Docs

- https://ratmath.com/finance/llms-full.txt: every page below as Markdown, each with a runnable example
- Pages: index (Overview), reference (Reference), explore (Explore), money (Money and rounding), dates (Dates and day counts), time-value (Time value of money), loans (Loans), cash-flows (Cash flows), bonds (Bonds), yield-curves (Yield curves), scenarios (Scenarios), uncertain (Uncertain inputs and repeated runs), portfolios (Portfolios), options (Options), life (Life contingencies)

## Example

```js
import { plan, amount, format, show, loan, irr, bond } from "@ratmath/finance";
const l = loan({ principal: 250000, rate: "6%", periods: 360 });
console.log("payment", show(l.payment, 2), " exactly", show(l.exactPayment, 8), "before rounding");
console.log("last payment", show(l.finalPayment, 2), " total interest", format(l.totals.interest));
console.log("in floating point, 0.1 + 0.2 =", 0.1 + 0.2, "; here:", String(amount("0.1").add(amount("0.2"))));
const two = irr([-1000, 2300, -1320]);
console.log("rates of return of −1000, +2300, −1320:", two.rates.map((r) => r.text).join(" and "), "—", two.note);
const b = bond({ coupon: "5%", periods: 20 });
console.log("bond at a 6% yield:", show(b.price("6%").clean, 6), " duration", show(b.duration("6%").macaulay, 4), "years");
plan.map((p) => `${p.phase}. ${p.contents}`)
```
